props.gloss_en: one verse: David rose at midnight (Ps 119:62)
the verse: 'I rose with the neshef and cried out' (Ps 119:147) -- David rose at neshef
the stam's premise: this neshef is evening, from 'in the neshef, in the evening of the day' (Prov 7:9)
R' Acha: David meant -- midnight never passed me by in sleep (sometimes he rose at neshef, but never later than midnight)
R' Zeira: until midnight David dozed like a horse; from then on he roused himself like a lion
Rav Ashi: until midnight David engaged in Torah; from then on in songs and praises
the verse: 'and David smote them from the neshef until the evening of the next day' (I Sam 30:17)
(entertained) the verse means from one evening to the next evening -- so neshef is evening after all
Rava: there are two neshefs -- the night departs and day comes (morning), the day departs and night comes (evening)
the verse: 'about midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt' (Ex 11:4) -- Moshe's 'about'
(entertained) it was the Holy One Himself who said 'about midnight' to Moshe
God said 'at midnight'; Moshe himself came and said 'about midnight'
Moshe knew exactly when midnight was (denied by the stam at 3b.28 -- אלמא מספקא ליה; asserted by R' Zeira at 4a.4)
David knew exactly when midnight was (R' Zeira, 4a.4)
David had a sign for midnight: a lyre hung over his bed; when midnight came the north wind blew through it and it played of itself, and he rose at once and studied Torah until dawn

at dawn the sages of Israel came in: your people need sustenance -- go and sustain one another -- a handful does not sate a lion, a pit is not filled from its own rim -- go and stretch out your hands in a troop
at once they take counsel with Achitofel, consult the Sanhedrin, and ask the Urim veTumim (and only then, 4a.2, the general Yoav)
the verse: 'and after Achitofel, Benayahu son of Yehoyada and Evyatar, and the general of the king's army, Yoav' (I Chr 27:34)
Achitofel in the verse stands for the adviser
the verse: 'and the counsel of Achitofel which he counselled in those days was as one who inquires of the word of God' (II Sam 16:23)
Benayahu ben Yehoyada in the verse stands for the Sanhedrin
Evyatar in the verse stands for the Urim veTumim
the verse: 'and Benayahu ben Yehoyada was over the Kereti and the Peleti' (II Sam 20:23)
why are they called Kereti and Peleti? Kereti because they cut [decide] their words; Peleti because their words are wondrous
the verse: 'awake, my glory; awake, harp and lyre; I will awaken the dawn' (Ps 57:9)
the lyre was there to wake him from his sleep (not to tell him the hour)
Moshe reasoned: lest Pharaoh's astrologers err [about the moment] and say 'Moshe is a liar' -- so he said 'about midnight'
the maxim: teach your tongue to say 'I do not know', lest you be caught in a falsehood
Rav Ashi: Moshe stood at midnight of the 13th going into the 14th, and said: tomorrow, at [a moment] like midnight now, I go out -- כחצות is a comparison, not an approximation

supports.gloss_en: מאי קרא? ואחרי אחיתפל בניהו בן יהוידע ואביתר ושר צבא למלך יואב -- the verse's order is the aggada's order: adviser, Sanhedrin, Urim veTumim, general
וכן הוא אומר: ועצת אחיתפל אשר יעץ... כאשר ישאל איש בדבר האלהים
וכן הוא אומר: ובניהו בן יהוידע על הכרתי ועל הפלתי -- the Kereti and Peleti being the Sanhedrin
מאי קרא? עורה כבודי עורה הנבל וכנור אעירה שחר -- the harp and lyre have woken [me], and I will now be awake until dawn
דאמר מר: למד לשונך לומר איני יודע, שמא תתבדה ותאחז -- Moshe hedged as the maxim counsels

objections.gloss_en: ודוד בפלגא דליליא הוה קאי? מאורתא הוה קאי! דכתיב קדמתי בנשף ואשועה -- and neshef is evening (Prov 7:9)

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר רב אושעיא אמר רבי אחא: הכי קאמר דוד -- midnight never passed me in sleep; he rose by neshef when he could, but never slept past midnight
until midnight he dozed like a horse, from then on he roused himself like a lion -- both verses describe one night
until midnight Torah (קדמתי בנשף... לדברך), from midnight songs and praises (חצות לילה אקום להודות לך)

objections.gloss_en: ונשף אורתא הוא? הא נשף צפרא הוא! דכתיב ויכם דוד מהנשף ועד הערב למחרתם -- מאי לאו מצפרא ועד ליליא?

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אמר רבא: תרי נשפי הוו -- the word names both transitions, so Prov 7:9's neshef is evening and I Sam 30:17's is morning

objections.gloss_en: ודוד מי הוה ידע פלגא דליליא אימת? השתא משה רבינו לא הוה ידע -- כחצות הלילה; God said בחצות and Moshe said כחצות, so Moshe was uncertain -- ודוד הוה ידע?!

answered_by.gloss_en: דוד סימנא הוה ליה -- the lyre over his bed played of itself at midnight (R' Shimon Chasida via Rav Acha bar Bizna)
משה לעולם הוה ידע, ודוד נמי הוה ידע -- the premise is denied: both knew
Moshe spoke at midnight of the 13th: 'tomorrow, at [a moment] like midnight now' -- כחצות is a comparison, so no uncertainty was ever expressed

objections.gloss_en: וכיון דדוד הוה ידע, כנור למה ליה?

answered_by.gloss_en: לאתעורי משנתיה -- to wake him from his sleep

objections.gloss_en: וכיון דמשה הוה ידע, למה ליה למימר כחצות?

answered_by.gloss_en: משה קסבר: שמא יטעו אצטגניני פרעה ויאמרו משה בדאי הוא -- דאמר מר: למד לשונך לומר איני יודע
